findings.namedBuyers: Ali LeBlanc, CMP, CIS — Director, Global Event Operations; best organizational route to identify hotel sourcing responsibility. Ellen Jensen — Chief Operating Officer; senior escalation for portfolio-level supplier relationships. Both are named on Canadian Institute’s official management page; neither is publicly established as this edition’s hotel-contract signatory. Rebecca Nobrega, Senior Conference Producer, publicly promoted and recapped the 2026 edition; useful historical programme introduction, but 2027 assignment and accommodation authority are unverified. Co-chairs are programme leaders, not verified hotel buyers.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced January 28–29, 2027; the agenda separately identifies both main-conference activity dates. One King West Hotel & Residence, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This is within the requested horizon. No officially announced 2028 edition was located; do not extrapolate dates.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel specifications: a 75+ attendee professional legal conference is plausibly compatible in meeting scale with Radisson Blu’s approximately 240-theatre largest room and 157 guestrooms, subject to actual setup and breakout needs. Attendance is not overnight room demand. The current venue already houses the conference and offers lodging, so realistic Radisson roles are unproven small delegate/speaker groups, VIP lodging or requested supplemental rooms—not exclusive housing. This is an urban professional conference, not a demonstrated resort programme or extended-stay relocation lead. No room-block size or length of stay can be inferred. Do not offer catered side meetings or receptions until hotel restaurant/lounge and catering operations are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: The edition-specific venue page confirms One King West Hotel & Residence, 1 King St W, Toronto, ON M5H 1A1. This is Toronto proper, downtown, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. It is a competing hotel and the published accommodation incumbent; no evidence of an open venue competition.
findings.historicalRotation: 2024: January 17–18, One King West Hotel, Toronto, confirmed by GALA and organizer-authored ACI event notice. 2025: January 27–28 main conference confirmed by co-chair Harris + co.; venue listed as One King West by secondary directory only. That directory includes January 29, possibly additional programming, but that extension is unverified. 2026: January 28–29 at One King West Hotel & Residence, Toronto, confirmed by event producer promotion and the official 2026 retrospective. 2027 returns to the same hotel. Evidence supports repeated Toronto/One King West use, not destination rotation. Conflicting third-party 2025 January 15–16 dates are not adopted.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific host-hotel block, booked directly with One King West Hotel & Residence, the only hotel named on the official venue/accommodation page. Exact wording: “Canadian Institute is pleased to offer our delegates a limited number of hotel rooms at a negotiated rate.” Delegates must contact the hotel directly and quote “Block code: 270125CIAM.” Published cutoff: January 13, 2027; thereafter OR when the block fills, availability and rate are no longer guaranteed. Reservations: 1-866-470-KING (5464) or 416-548-8100. No published block quantity, room rate, housing bureau, second hotel, overflow allocation or open RFP was found. A conditional block-fill warning is not evidence of actual sell-out.
findings.organizationStructure: Canadian Institute is the conference organizer, a commercial conference business in the C5 Group of Companies alongside American Conference Institute and C5 Group; not evidenced as a membership association. One King West is the host venue/accommodation supplier, not the event owner. No external PCO, DMC or housing agency is identified in the reviewed edition materials.
findings.competitiveLimitations: One King West has the published meeting venue and negotiated accommodation block. Repeated hosting in 2024, 2026 and 2027 indicates an incumbent relationship; 2025 venue evidence is secondary. Livestream registration offers a remote alternative. The advertised 75+ attendees do not establish nonlocal participation or paid room nights. No sourced sell-out, displacement, waitlist, overflow need or unmet demand was located.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Canadian Institute’s customer experience team at customerservice@canadianinstitute.com or 1-877-927-7936, requesting referral to Ali LeBlanc or the operations lead for this conference. Confirm whether 2027 supplemental rooms are needed, who controls hotel sourcing, existing block pickup/cutoff arrangements and when a future venue/hotel decision becomes contestable. Offer a right-sized room-only option only if a need is confirmed; otherwise seek a future sourcing introduction. Use Ellen Jensen for portfolio-level escalation, not an asserted event-buyer role. Verify hotel catering capability before proposing food-and-beverage functions.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Low/conditional as of November 16, 2026: the 2027 meeting venue and accommodation offer are committed to One King West. Do not label hotel sourcing open or solicit replacement of a contracted venue as though accessible. Ask operations only whether supplemental hotel capacity or speaker/VIP lodging outside the host block is needed; even a block cutoff does not establish accessible overflow.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeat editions justify relationship development for the next genuinely contestable cycle or a broader Canadian Institute Toronto programme. No 2028 event date, venue tender or sourcing window is publicly verified. Explore future room-only or complete mid-size conference proposals only after learning renewal timing, room pickup, venue requirements and incumbent constraints.
